questions.q: What makes Triton Inference Server different from vLLM and TensorRT-LLM?
options: Triton only works with image models, never LLMs
Triton is a general-purpose, framework-agnostic server that can host many different model frameworks (including vLLM and TensorRT-LLM) through pluggable backends
Triton is a replacement for GPUs entirely
Triton can only run one model at a time, never multiple
questions.explain: Triton is framework-agnostic: it defines one consistent request/response protocol and uses pluggable backends to execute models built with many different frameworks, including vLLM and TensorRT-LLM.

options: The database that stores user accounts
The component that knows how to actually execute a particular kind of model (e.g., the vLLM backend, the TensorRT-LLM backend, or the PyTorch backend)
A type of GPU made specifically for Triton
The client library used to send requests
questions.explain: A backend is the pluggable piece of Triton responsible for executing a specific model framework, which is how one Triton server can host many different kinds of models.

options: A group of identical GPUs working together
A chained pipeline of multiple models (e.g., preprocessing, main model, postprocessing) served as one logical request to the client
A single model trained on multiple datasets
A backup copy of a model repository
questions.explain: A model ensemble lets Triton chain multiple models into one pipeline internally, so a client makes a single request while Triton handles routing between the steps.

questions.q: What does a Triton model repository contain?
options: A single binary file for the entire server
A directory structure where each subdirectory is one model, with versioned model files and a config.pbtxt configuration file
Only client-side JavaScript code
A list of GPU driver versions
questions.explain: Triton organizes models on disk as a model repository, where each model has its own subdirectory containing versioned files and a config.pbtxt that specifies backend, batching, and instance settings.

questions.q: How does running a vLLM server "inside" Triton (via the vLLM backend) differ from running vLLM standalone?
options: It is functionally identical with no added benefit
It removes vLLM's continuous batching entirely
It gains Triton's shared infrastructure, such as metrics, health checks, and multi-model hosting, on top of vLLM's own serving logic
It requires abandoning the OpenAI-compatible API
questions.explain: Running vLLM through Triton's vLLM backend adds Triton's shared serving infrastructure — metrics, health checks, model management, and multi-model hosting — around vLLM's own scheduling and memory management.
